keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1300, the Hurmuzi merchants cast off Persian overlordship' and in 1301 moved to the island of Jerun; 'The Hurmuzi rulers developed Qalhat on the Omani coast in order to control both sides of the entrance to the Persian Gulf' (undated, bridged at 1300 at confidence 1). The Hormuz Island page: the mainland principality 'held territory on both sides of the strait'. Bahrain: Hormuz was nominally overlord of the Jabrids (undated; not drawn).

The Portuguese 'occupied Ormuz from 1515 to 1622' and the infobox calls the kingdom a 'vassal state of Portugal (1515-1622)'; the island is drawn as the Portuguese holding, as in the portuguese-empire dossier's 1515 gain ('Hormuz (Huwala state)'); the kings (Turan Shah IV 1514-1522 to Mohammed Shah IV 1610-1622) remain.

ledger.note: Bridge at confidence 1 (page silent on the year): the kingdom was founded 'after the collapse of the Buyid kingdom' in the 11th century by Muhammad Diramku, who emigrated from Oman to the Iranian coast; the Kerman Seljuk emir Badr Isa of Hormuz had submitted to Qavurt before 1073 (Qavurt page).

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: Undated, placed at 1300 (Persian overlordship cast off): 'The Hurmuzi rulers developed Qalhat on the Omani coast in order to control both sides of the entrance to the Persian Gulf.'

1301: the capital moves to Jarun, the island of Hormuz. 'Instead, in 1301, the inhabitants ... moved to the neighbouring island of Jerun' (the page also says 1300 and that Mir Bahrudin 'obtained it from Neyn (Na'im), King of Keys (Kish)', in a passage flagged as possibly unreliable and undated). The Hormuz Island page: the ruler moved 'to evade attacks by Mongolian and Turkish groups from the interior'.
1301: the court moves from Old Hormuz (Naband) to the island of Jarun.

September 1507: Afonso de Albuquerque lands on the island of Hormuz ('In September 1507, the Portuguese Afonso de Albuquerque landed on the island'); the Hormuz Island page: he 'captured the island in 1507'.
1515: the Portuguese take Ormuz ('After seizing Hormuz in 1515'; 'from 1515 to 1622') and the kingdom becomes their vassal.

1515: Hormuz island passes to the Portuguese, who built the Fort of Our Lady of the Conception there (Hormuz Island page); the portuguese-empire dossier records the conquest in 1515. The kings remain as vassals to 1622.

ledger.note: 1622: the Safavids, helped by the English, conquer the kingdom ('conquered the kingdom in 1622'; infobox 'Safavid conquest: 1622'). Muscat, formerly a dependency of Hormuz, is named by the page as a successor state.

ledger.note: 1622: the kingdom ends; Shah Abbas I 'shifted the Gulf trade to Bandar Abbas, located on the mainland'.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Hormuz
wars.outcome: Albuquerque landed on the island in September 1507; the Portuguese occupied Ormuz in 1515 and held it to 1622 with the king as vassal.
wars.note: The Hormuz Island page says the island was captured in 1507; the Kingdom of Hormuz page dates the occupation to 1515.

wars.name: Portuguese invasion of Bahrain
wars.outcome: The Hormuz page says Hormuz 'jointly participated in the 1521 invasion of Bahrain that ended Jabrid rule'; the Jabrids page says Muqrin fell in battle in Bahrain against a Portuguese invasion and does not mention Hormuz. Bahrain is not drawn as Hormuz land.

wars.name: Capture of Ormuz (1622)
wars.outcome: Anglo-Persian forces took the Portuguese garrison at Hormuz Island in 1622; the Hormuz page says the Safavids 'conquered the kingdom in 1622' with English help.
wars.note: The Capture of Ormuz page opened is only a disambiguation page (year 1622, no month); the details come from the Kingdom of Hormuz page.

certainty.note: A coastal city-state: a disc round Minab and, from 1301, the island of Hormuz and Qalhat on the Omani coast; no frontier on any page opened, and the reach to Bahrain and Muscat is undated.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). The pages are thin: four opened (one a disambiguation page); a gap-filler should open the 'Portuguese Ormuz' material under another title and the Persian-language history. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
The foundation year is a bridge at confidence 1: the page gives only 'the 11th century'. Not settled: Hormuz's reach in the Gulf (Qeshm, Larak, Bahrain, Qatif, Muscat, Julfar, Khor Fakkan, Socotra are either absent or undated on the pages); the 'zenith' reach to Bahrain is marked [citation needed] on the page; the Jabrids page does not make Hormuz their overlord; the 1300/1301 conflict for the move; the Mahmud Qalhati reign 1249-1286 'cutting dependence ties with Kerman and the Salghurids' (undated step); Kerman Seljuk, Salghurid and Ilkhanid overlordships are the suzerains' tints (kerman-seljuk-sultanate and salghurids carry none).
The nabhani-dynasty dossier names 'Kingdom of Hormuz' as holder of the Omani coast at one point (undated).
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Minab, Qalhat.
